children: A win for Germany's far-right AfD party in a regional election is unlikely to impede economic reform, Holger Schmieding at Berenberg says in a note. The AfD's support more than doubled in the Saxony-Anhalt election, while chancellor Friedrich Merz's vote share tumbled. "The unpopularity of Merz and concerns about the pension and other reforms which his government is planning to raise Germany's growth potential played a significant role," Schmieding says. However, Merz and his coalition government will likely continue until the end of their term in early 2029, he adds. And while planned pro-growth reforms may be softened at the margins, the bulk should still be passed this autumn. "The planned increases in defense and infrastructure spending should also not be affected." (don.forbes@wsj.com)
